title: Induction before cleaning work starts
audience: New and returning cleaners, anyone moved to a new site or a new task, and the supervisors who run inductions, in any cleaning-group business.
learningOutcomes: Name the topics an induction must cover before a worker starts cleaning on a site.
Find the chemical register, the safety data sheets, the risk assessment records and the emergency details for a site during an induction walk-through.
Explain when an induction, or the part of it that has changed, must be repeated.
Complete an induction record that states the tasks the worker is cleared for and the tasks they are not yet cleared for.

instruction.heading: Status of this lesson
instruction.body: The uploaded source gives the title of an induction annex but not its text, so this lesson is a general outline written by the team and is not the business's own induction policy. It must be replaced with the annex text once that text is supplied and reviewed. Nothing in this lesson sets how long an induction takes, and nothing in it grants a licence, a certificate or any authority to do regulated work.

instruction.heading: Why the induction comes first
instruction.body: A new worker does not yet know the hazards on a site, where the safety information is kept, or who to call when something goes wrong. The induction passes that knowledge from the supervisor to the worker before the first task, rather than during it. It also creates a record that the information was given, which protects both the worker and the business if a question arises later.

instruction.heading: The topics an induction covers
instruction.body: A cleaning induction usually covers the standard operating procedures that apply to the worker's tasks, the chemicals in use and where their labels and safety data sheets are kept, the protective gear each task needs, the colour-coded equipment system and where it is stored, and the hazards that belong to the site itself, such as wet floors, fixed plant and restricted areas. It also covers the fire exits, the assembly point, the first-aid point, how to report an injury, a near miss or damage, and who the supervisor is and how to reach them.

instruction.heading: Walking the site
instruction.body: The supervisor takes the worker around the site rather than only describing it. At each stop the worker sees the chemical store, the sharps and waste points, the equipment store, the amenities, the exits, and the areas where entry is restricted. The worker should be invited to ask questions at every stop. The supervisor then asks the worker to point out one hazard and its control, in the worker's own words, before moving on.

instruction.heading: The induction record and sign-off
instruction.body: The induction record names the worker, the date, the supervisor and the site. It lists the topics covered and the tasks the worker is cleared to do at that point. Where a worker is cleared for some tasks but not others, the record says so in plain terms. Both the worker and the supervisor sign it, and the record is kept with the business's training records. The policy the induction follows is recorded by reference, using the business's own policy reference.

instruction.heading: When an induction must be repeated
instruction.body: Repeat the induction, or the part of it that has changed, after a change of task, a change of site, a new chemical or machine, a new hazard on the site, or any incident that shows the worker may not have understood something. A worker who was inducted for one task is not cleared for a different task until the part of the induction about that task has been covered and recorded.

instruction.heading: Legal position
instruction.body: Work health and safety law in each state and territory sets the duties of a business to inform, instruct and train its workers. Check them against the law of each jurisdiction before the induction is finalised.

procedure: Before the first shift, gather the site's induction checklist, the site map, the chemical register and the emergency details for the site.
Introduce the supervisor, the work that is planned, and the tasks the worker is expected to do on that day.
Walk the site with the worker, stopping at the chemical store, the waste and sharps points, the equipment store, the amenities, the exits and each restricted area.
At each stop, name the hazard and its control, and ask the worker to repeat one of them in their own words.
Show the worker where each chemical's data sheet is kept, and ask them to fetch one of them.
Explain how to report an injury, a near miss or damage on the day it happens, and where the forms are kept.
Explain which tasks the worker is cleared for at this stage and which tasks they must not do yet.
Complete the induction record, listing the topics covered and the tasks cleared, and ask the worker to sign it.
Sign the record as the supervisor, and file it with the business's training records.
Set a date or a trigger for a refresher, and record the date or the trigger on the record.

workedExamples.situation: A new cleaner starts on Monday at a site that has a plant room the public must never enter, a chemical store, and a stairwell that stays wet until mid-morning.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What must the induction cover before the cleaner starts work on the stairwell?
workedExamples.reasoning: The induction must show the restricted plant room, the chemical store and the controls for the wet stairwell, including the warning signs placed before the work begins. The worker has to see the hazard and its control on the site before the first task, and the record must show that the stairwell is one of the tasks cleared.

workedExamples.situation: A worker was inducted for hard-floor work and is now asked to clean the windows on the same site the following week.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Does the earlier induction cover the window work?
workedExamples.reasoning: No. The change of task calls for the part of the induction about window work: its chemicals, its protective equipment, its barriers and the stop-work boundary for height work in “Window cleaning from the ground and with extension equipment”. The record must show that window work is now cleared, and the clearance should wait until that part has been covered.

workedExamples.situation: In the first week, a cleaner reports a needle stick in a washroom. The supervisor finds that the cleaner did not know where the sharps container was kept.
workedExamples.reasoning: The supervisor makes sure the injury is treated and reported under the business's process, and checks the induction record. The gap is in the topic about sharps locations, so that topic is repeated before the worker goes back to washroom work. The sharps controls are covered in “Sharps and body fluids: policy, reporting and records” and the spill and sharps procedure in “Body fluid spill and sharps clean-up (high-risk: trained workers only)”.

equipmentAndPpe: The induction checklist and the induction record form.
A site map that shows exits, the assembly point, the first-aid point and the restricted areas.
Access to the chemical register, the safety data sheets and the risk assessments for the site.
The protective gear for the worker's tasks, shown to the worker in use.

commonErrors.error: Treating the induction as a form to sign rather than a walk-through with questions.
commonErrors.prevention: Walk the site, stop at each hazard, and ask the worker to name a hazard and its control.

commonErrors.error: Signing the record for the whole job when the worker has seen only part of the work.
commonErrors.prevention: List the tasks the worker is cleared for, and clear each new task separately once it is covered.

commonErrors.error: Not repeating the induction after a change of task, site or hazard.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep a trigger list beside the induction record and check it at every change.

commonErrors.error: Showing where the safety data sheets are kept without checking that the worker can find one.
commonErrors.prevention: Ask the worker to fetch a named safety data sheet during the walk-through.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: An induction does not authorise a worker to do a task that needs a licence or a specific training qualification. Where a task needs one, the record must state that the worker is not cleared for it.
The duty to inform, instruct and train workers, and any content or length an induction must meet in each state and territory, must be checked against the rules that apply where the work is done.

Site hazards, including wet floors, restricted plant rooms and chemical stores, must be shown to a worker before the first task in that area. Do not let a worker start in an area that has not been shown to them.
Every injury, near miss and damage event is reported on the day under the business's own process.

qualityStandard: Every topic on the induction checklist is covered and recorded.
The worker can find the chemical register, a safety data sheet and the first-aid point without help.
The clearance record matches the tasks the worker actually does, and it lists any task the worker is not cleared for.
The record is signed by the worker and the supervisor and is filed with the training records.
documentationEvidence: Completed induction record showing the date, the site, the supervisor, the topics covered and the tasks cleared.
Signatures of the worker and the supervisor.
Record of each repeat or partial induction, with the trigger that caused it.
The policy reference the induction followed, using the business's own reference.
summary: The induction gives the worker the site's hazards and controls before the first task, not during it.
Walk the site and ask the worker to name a hazard and its control at each stop.
Clear a worker only for the tasks the induction has covered, and record any task they are not cleared for.
Repeat the induction, or the changed part of it, after a change of task, site, chemical, machine, hazard or incident.

knowledgeChecks.question: Before a new cleaner starts a task on a site, what must the induction have covered?
options: The worker's hourly rate and the rostered hours and the bus route to the site
The name of the client's head office and the head office phone number
The site hazards and their controls for the worker's tasks, shown on the site

knowledgeChecks.question: A worker was inducted for hard-floor work and must now clean windows on the same site. What is the correct response?
options: Clear the worker for window work once the window part of the induction is covered and recorded
The earlier induction covers it, so no further record is needed and it applies to every task on site
Let the worker begin window work and cover the induction later in the week if the supervisor is happy

knowledgeChecks.question: When must a refresher or a partial re-induction be run?
options: Only once a year, on the same date and not at any other time, even after a change of site
After a change of task, site or hazard, and after an incident that shows a gap in understanding
Only when the worker asks for one and only after the first full month at work on site
